scenes.question: What do the Dispatcher Tools in the AEM as a Cloud Service SDK provide?
scenes.heading: They provide a vanilla project file structure, validation tooling, and a Docker image for local Dispatcher

scenes.question: Which Dispatcher mode is recommended in AEM as a Cloud Service, and how is it activated?
scenes.heading: Flexible mode is recommended and is activated by the file opt-in/USE_SOURCES_DIRECTLY
scenes.body: The source says flexible mode is recommended, is the default for archetype 28 and higher, and is activated by the file opt-in/USE_SOURCES_DIRECTLY.

scenes.question: What limitation applied in legacy mode that flexible mode removes?

scenes.question: What is the main difference between conf.d and conf.dispatcher.d in a Cloud Service Dispatcher project?
scenes.heading: conf.d holds Apache configuration, while conf.dispatcher.d holds Dispatcher configuration
scenes.body: The speech says the project Dispatcher folder has two main subfolders: conf.d for Apache configuration and conf.dispatcher.d for Dispatcher configuration.

scenes.question: How should a virtual host or farm be enabled in Cloud Service Dispatcher configuration?
scenes.heading: Create it in the available folder and enable it with a relative symbolic link in the enabled folder
scenes.body: The source says a virtual host or farm is created in the available folder and enabled by a relative symbolic link in the enabled folder, and specifically warns not to copy default.vhost directly into enabled_vhosts.

scenes.question: Which aliases must at least one virtual host match so Dispatcher invalidation works in Cloud Service local setups?
scenes.heading: At least one virtual host must match *.local, localhost, and 127.0.0.1
scenes.body: The speech says at least one virtual host must match the ServerAlias values *.local, localhost, and 127.0.0.1 because they are needed for Dispatcher invalidation.
